references.text: The skin, all the flesh, the head, the legs, the entrails, and the dung of the sin offering bull were to be burned outside the camp. This is the original regulation that Leviticus 9:11 follows.
The bull shall be burned just as the first bull was burned—outside the camp. The same practice of burning flesh and skin outside the camp applies.
At the consecration of the priests, the bull's skin, flesh, and dung were burned with fire outside the camp, exactly as described in chapter 9.
On the Day of Atonement, the sin offering's skin, flesh, and dung were to be burned outside the camp. The same principle of burning outside the camp applies.
The red heifer was to be completely burned, including its skin and flesh, outside the camp.
Hebrews explains that the animals whose blood was brought into the sanctuary were burned outside the camp. Jesus also suffered outside the city gate to sanctify the people with his own blood.
